title: Modi Felicitates Asian Games Medalists, Backs India's 2036 Olympics Bid
excerpt: India's 85-medal contingent, including both gold-winning cricket teams, was honoured in New Delhi as Modi set out a 2030 Commonwealth Games to 2036 Olympics roadmap.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi felicitated India's Asian Games contingent in New Delhi on October 15 after the team won 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze — for a fourth-place finish at Aichi-Nagoya.
  • Both gold-winning cricket teams were honoured, with the men's side led by Shreyas Iyer and the women's side presenting Modi a signed jersey.
  • Women athletes won 38 medals, including 11 gold, and debutants won 41 medals, with first-ever Asian Games medals in mixed martial arts, soft tennis and sailing events.
  • Modi restated India's bid to host the 2036 Olympics, with the 2030 Commonwealth Games as the intermediate test.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met India's Asian Games medal winners at the Major Dhyan Chand Stadium in New Delhi on Thursday and used the felicitation to restate the country's ambition to host the 2036 Olympic Games. The contingent finished fourth at the Aichi-Nagoya Games with 85 medals, and Modi told the athletes their results belonged to the whole country.

The ceremony covered the full contingent, not a single sport. Both cricket teams that won gold were present — the men's T20 side led by Shreyas Iyer, which had played a T20 international against the West Indies a day earlier, and the women's team led during the tournament by Harmanpreet Kaur. Kaur presented Modi with a jersey signed by the women's team, and her successor Smriti Mandhana joined the photographs, according to coverage of the event by Cricket News.

"We are bidding for 2036 Olympics and it is our resolve that we will host the games."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister

A broader medal base

India's total of 85 medals was below the 106 won at Hangzhou, but the distribution was wider. Debutants accounted for 41 medals, and Modi highlighted first medals in sports where India had not previously reached an Asian Games podium, including mixed martial arts, soft tennis and certain sailing events. He described those firsts as evidence of a changing sporting culture rather than strength in a few traditional disciplines alone.

https://x.com/Olympics/status/2106417316221313040

Women athletes contributed 38 medals, 11 of them gold. Modi singled out the women's hockey team, whose gold ended a 44-year wait, and noted golds for both hockey teams and both kabaddi teams. Archers won five gold medals, and there were also returns after long gaps — a weightlifting medal after 28 years and marathon success for the first time since 1982, he said in his address reported by Nation Press.

Individual athletes brought personal mementoes. Recurve archer Kumkum Mohod, 17, who won two gold medals and a silver, presented a bow. Golfer Pranavi Urs presented a glove and a framed golf ball. Officials present included International Cricket Council chairman Jay Shah and Indian Olympic Association president P.T. Usha.

The system behind the medals

Modi credited a decade of investment through the Target Olympic Podium Scheme, which funds elite athletes, and Khelo India, which runs more than 1,000 centres nationally and a village-level talent search. He pointed to monthly allowances, overseas training support and upgraded tracks, pools and multipurpose halls as the infrastructure intended to keep producing medalists between Games cycles.

That system will now be judged against a hosting timetable as much as a medals table. India submitted a letter of intent for 2036 to the International Olympic Committee's Future Host Commission on October 1, 2024, and remains in dialogue alongside Germany, Hungary, Qatar, South Korea, South Africa and Türkiye. No host decision has been made.

What happens next

The 2030 Commonwealth Games, which India will host, is the intermediate milestone Modi cited before 2036. It will test venue operations, transport and security at multi-sport scale, and its delivery will form part of the case India makes to the IOC.

For diaspora fans, the immediate story is simpler: a contingent that included repeat cricket golds, a breakthrough women's hockey title and medals in new sports was recognised as a collective national team, not as separate federations. The next test is whether the broader base Modi praised converts into a larger haul — and a credible hosting bid — over the next decade.
